name: St Albans Church
reason: Tourism board page names the oldest public building in Kingscote (1884 chancel) and two stained-glass windows incl. one depicting island elements. For: named interior detail, heritage. Against: small local church, one source, ~15 min visit; no stated public opening.

name: Strawbridge Point
reason: Tourism page is a geomorphology note: sandy point and tidal flats opposite American River, road ends at the point, 4WD on beach. No sight or activity named; not a guide-named stop.

name: Tadpole Cove Walk (Cape Gantheaume)
reason: Agency-sourced walk (DEW/NPWS) to a lookout above Tadpole Cove past early-settler threshing floor and cottage ruins; osprey watching. Distinct named walk.

name: Timber Creek Walk (Cape Gantheaume)
reason: Agency-sourced walk at Murray Lagoon in Cape Gantheaume Conservation Park for swamp birdlife (ducks, swans, waders); named walk. Seasonal flooding in winter. Overlaps the Bald Hill/Curley Creek area but is a separate trail.

name: Old Cemetery Kingscote
reason: Tourism page: South Australia's oldest cemetery, preserved, holding 1836 South Australia Company settlers. For: genuine heritage site, free and open. Against: single source, short visit, closer to a memorial/cemetery than an attraction.

name: Curley Creek Hike (Cape Gantheaume)
reason: Agency-sourced hike along Murray Lagoon edge in Cape Gantheaume Conservation Park (6 km from park office) with birdlife and vegetation; named long walk, distinct from Bald Hill walk. Winter flooding.

name: Island Beehive
reason: Honey producer and farm-gate shop (Kangaroo Island Ligurian Bee Co): a business/operator, not a place.

name: Bay of Shoals Beach
reason: Tourism page describes a shallow tidal bay with sand flats, generally unsuitable for swimming or beach use; no visitor sight or activity named.

name: Beyeria Walk
reason: Agency-sourced 1.5 km, 30 minute interpretive mallee walk (20 signs) in Beyeria Conservation Park; named walk.

name: Boxing Bay Beach
reason: Tourism page calls it an isolated bay mainly used by local fishers, vehicle track access; no guide-named draw.

name: Brown Beach
reason: Tourism board names a sheltered, easily accessible family beach for swimming, snorkelling and shell fossicking with camping ground, BBQs and toilets; second-tier beach.

name: Brownlow Beach
reason: Describes a small beachfront settlement with narrow beach and sand flats unsuitable for swimming; nothing to see or do named.

name: Cape Willoughby Heritage Trail
reason: duplicate of Cape Willoughby Lighthouse: the 1.9 km heritage loop starts at the lightstation visitor centre and is part of that visit.

name: Bales Beach
reason: Tourism page: accessible surf and walking beach next to Seal Bay inside an aquatic reserve protecting sea lion breeding; small car park. Second-tier beach, short stop.

name: Artworks Gallery
reason: Community artists' gallery and shop selling art and craft; a venue/shop (open only when flags are out), giant octopus sculpture not enough.

name: Bald Hill Walk (Cape Gantheaume)
reason: Agency-sourced walk to Bald Hill with spectacular views over Murray Lagoon and wetland bird watching in Cape Gantheaume Conservation Park.

name: Kangaroo Island Oysters
reason: Oyster farm gate and eatery: a producer/business, not a place of interest.

name: Kangaroo Island Providore
reason: Food producer/cafe: a business, not a distinct attraction.

name: Emu Ridge Cafe and Cellar Door
reason: Cafe and cellar door at a distillery: business/cellar door, no guide singles it out as a destination.

name: Kangaroo Island Source
reason: Produce store/cafe: a business.

name: The Rocks Cafe (Flinders Chase)
reason: Cafe at the Flinders Chase visitor centre: a cafe, not an attraction.

name: Ragini Dey Indian Queen
reason: Restaurant: a business, not an attraction.

name: Admirals Arch
reason: Wikivoyage See: rock arch with New Zealand fur seal colony reached by boardwalk and steps in Flinders Chase; headline draw.

name: Cape Borda Lighthouse
reason: Wikivoyage lists the 1858 Cape Borda Lighthouse with tours; remote but a named lightstation to visit.

name: Cape du Couedic
reason: duplicate of Admirals Arch: the cape is where Admirals Arch and the Cape du Couedic Lighthouse sit; Wikivoyage lists the arch and lighthouse separately and the headland adds no separate draw.

name: Cape Willoughby Lighthouse
reason: Wikivoyage lists South Australia's first lighthouse (1852) with tours to the top; agency page confirms visitor centre and views.

name: Flinders Chase National Park
reason: Wikivoyage and agency: Kangaroo Island's flagship national park (Remarkable Rocks, Admirals Arch, wildlife) with an entry fee; a place in its own right.

name: Independence replica and Rebuild Independence Project
reason: Tourism board American River page names the Independence replica at the town turnoff and the shed on the wharf where volunteers rebuild the ship. For: named heritage stop. Against: small volunteer project, one source, ~20 min, shed opening unclear.

name: Kangaroo Island Wildlife Park
reason: Wikivoyage See: walk-through wildlife park near Parndana with kangaroos coming to visitors.

name: Kelly Hill Caves
reason: Wikivoyage lists Kelly Hill Caves show-cave tours (daily, fee) in Kelly Hill Conservation Park.

name: Kingscote
reason: Wikivoyage and tourism board give Kingscote its own section: island's largest town, harbour and first European settlement of South Australia.

name: Little Sahara
reason: Wikivoyage Do: Little Sahara sandboarding dunes on the South Coast Road.

name: MacGillivray Post Office (Emu Ridge)
reason: A relocated post office building preserved on the grounds of Emu Ridge, a private distillery/cafe business; a corner of a business, not a distinct public place.

name: Parndana
reason: Tourism board gives Parndana its own destination page (central base, Soldier Settlement Museum, Australian Red Gum Gallery) and Wikivoyage lists it as one of four settlements; kept as a town, though thin.

name: Penneshaw
reason: Wikivoyage settlement and ferry arrival point with the Gateway visitor centre; tourism board has a Penneshaw and Dudley Peninsula section (penguin centre, museum).

name: Penneshaw Maritime and Folk Museum
reason: Wikivoyage lists it and tourism board describes a National Trust museum with maritime and folk displays; small museum a guide names.

name: Remarkable Rocks
reason: Wikivoyage See: wind-sculpted granite formations you can walk among, Flinders Chase; headline draw.

name: Seal Bay Conservation Park
reason: Wikivoyage See: Australian sea lion colony with guided beach tours, daily; headline draw.

name: The Cairn
reason: Tourism page: cairn marking the first Post Office site on Governor Wallen Drive, early settler remains and a walk up Flagstaff Hill with views over Backstairs Passage. For: a free walk with views and settlement heritage. Against: the cairn itself is a minor marker, one source, ~30 min.

name: Vivonne Bay
reason: southaustralia.com and Wikivoyage: long white beach once voted among Australia's best, jetty, south coast tour stop.
